intent: Compare private and state schools on paying business rates, and convey the potential annual revenue from requiring private schools to pay as state schools do.

requirements.question: How do private and state schools compare on paying business rates?

scope.measure: share paying business rates / additional revenue

requirements.question: What additional annual revenue could come from private schools paying as state schools do?

scope.measure: share paying business rates / additional revenue

units.claim: Private schools pay 0% of business rates, while state schools pay 100%.
accept: private schools pay none; state schools pay in full
an empty bar beside a full bar
reject: missing one of the two groups
units.evidence: Two bars: private at 0% and state at 100%.

units.claim: Requiring private schools to pay as state schools do could raise an additional £105m per year.
reject: a revenue figure without the £105m value
units.evidence: The £105m annotation is visible (not a bar).
